articles.title: Decision to arrest ex-Ukrainian Defense Minister Reznikov in absentia comes into effect
articles.summary: Reznikov is accused of committing particularly grave crimes against civilians in the Donbass region
articles.body: MOSCOW, November 21. /TASS/. The Moscow City Court has upheld the decision to arrest former Ukrainian Defense Minister Alexey Reznikov in absentia, according to documents seen by TASS. Reznikov is accused of committing particularly grave crimes against civilians in the Donbass region. Former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mikhail Fedorov is also a subject of the criminal case. Both individuals have been placed on an international wanted list.

articles.title: Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy’s hometown
articles.summary: About 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and businesses were damaged, according to Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of Kryvyi Rih’s city administration
articles.body: A Russian attack on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s hometown of Kryvyi Rih has killed two people and wounded 60 others, according to local officials. The strikes hit the central Ukrainian city on Friday night, killing a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman, while six children were among the injured. About 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and businesses were damaged, according to Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of Kryvyi Rih’s city administration. Vilkul said on Saturday that Russian forces launched further missiles after emergency workers arrived, hitting rescuers, medical personnel and utility crews. Footage released by Ukraine’s emergency services appeared to show additional strikes during the rescue operation. Russian attacks elsewhere in Ukraine killed two people in the southern Zaporizhia region, according to its governor. Russian authorities also reported six deaths, including a child, from a Ukrainian attack on a residential area in Russian-controlled Luhansk, an eastern Ukrainian region. The violence followed a separate incident on Friday in which two Russian missiles and a suspected drone landed in southeastern Poland, a member of NATO, the military alliance linking the United States, Canada and European countries. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incident on Friday as a deliberate provocation, questioning its timing alongside military exercises involving European countries preparing for a possible post-war security mission in Ukraine. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte condemned the airspace violation on Saturday and pledged that the alliance would defend Polish territory. The incidents have unfolded as US President Donald Trump seeks progress in negotiations with Moscow and Kyiv. Trump said on Friday, following talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in China, that the Russian leader wanted to end the war diplomatically. Zelenskyy, however, told reporters in Kyiv on Saturday that he remained less convinced than Washington that Putin was prepared to compromise. Moscow continues to demand Ukrainian withdrawal from the entire eastern Donbas region, which Kyiv refuses to surrender. Zelenskyy also reaffirmed Ukraine’s ambition to join NATO, while Washington has discussed offering Kyiv security guarantees resembling the alliance’s collective-defence commitments. Such guarantees remain under discussion as negotiations continue over how to end the war and protect Ukraine from future attacks.

Previously rejected Uzbek family ends 2-year church sanctuary after new asylum bid
articles.summary: According to the organization, church asylum coordinator Herman Stomphorst said Asylum Seekers (COA) is arranging accommodation for them
articles.body: The Uzbek Babayants family will leave the Open Hof church in Kampen within a few days, where they have received church sanctuary for the past two years. According to the organization, church asylum coordinator Herman Stomphorst said Asylum Seekers (COA) is arranging accommodation for them. “Until then, they may stay here in the church,” Stomphorst said shortly before the continuous church service ended on Saturday afternoon. The family of four children has lived in the Netherlands since 2014. Because they have now submitted a new residence application, the family may legally remain in the Netherlands for the duration of the procedure. The family itself chose to leave the church, supported by a ruling from the Council of State. In July, the Council of State ruled that three asylum-seeker families with children who have lived in the Netherlands for years and built lives here may stay. The highest administrative court determined that the minister must give greater weight to the interests of the children. For Stomphorst, Saturday is a tense day. “I worry that the procedure will take a very long time,” he said. “But I am reassured because the Council of State has been very clear.” At the same time, he is prepared for the possibility that things may not turn out well. “We are not naive. There is certainly a chance that the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (IND) will reject the application again. The Babayants family only submitted a new application this week, according to the family’s lawyer, Inge Zuidhoek, because it had to be properly prepared. Additional information was included about the family and their roots in the Netherlands. Zuidhoek hopes this new information will lead to a fresh assessment by the IND. “If it had no chance of success, I would not have submitted a new application,” she said.

Uzbekistan outlines CIS cooperation priorities for 2027
articles.summary: Participants discussed the development of interparliamentary cooperation, the harmonisation of national legislation and stronger engagement in the economic, social and humanitarian spheres
articles.body: Tashkent, Uzbekistan (UzDaily.uz) — A parliamentary delegation from Uzbekistan, led by Senate Chairperson of the Oliy Majlis Tanzila Narbayeva, took part in the 61st plenary session of the CIS Interparliamentary Assembly in the city of Avaza, Turkmenistan, the Senate’s press service said. Participants discussed the development of interparliamentary cooperation, the harmonisation of national legislation and stronger engagement in the economic, social and humanitarian spheres. In her address, Narbayeva outlined Uzbekistan’s efforts to incorporate model laws and recommendations adopted by the Interparliamentary Assembly into national legislation. She emphasised the importance of cooperation on protecting women from harassment and violence, digitalising healthcare, mutually recognising medical documents, and safeguarding citizens’ rights and interests. The Senate chairperson also presented proposals for priority areas of interparliamentary cooperation in 2027, when Uzbekistan will chair the CIS. The proposed priorities include improving the legal framework for joint investment and technology projects, reducing barriers to mutual trade, and strengthening cooperation in combating terrorism, extremism and cybercrime. Uzbekistan also proposed expanding interparliamentary ties in education and science. In addition, as 2027 has been declared the Year of Legal Education in the CIS, Narbayeva proposed holding a series of meetings under the auspices of the Assembly involving parliamentarians, lawyers, educators and young people.

Vance stops short of endorsing Trump’s claim that Iran was close to nuclear weapon
articles.summary: I didn’t say I was unhappy with it,” Trump said
articles.body: At a White House news conference on Friday, JD Vance stopped short of endorsing Donald Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to obtaining a nuclear weapon in February that it was essential for the US to go to war with the Islamic republic. In the White House briefing room, Trump was asked about reporting this week that he was unhappy with the US vice-president’s statement blaming Republican losses in the midterm elections on the Iran war. “I didn’t say I was unhappy with it,” Trump said. “I thought the statement was fine, except I would have had one other thing, that if it were asked, I would have said that: ‘Would you do it again?’ And absolutely, the answer is yes, because we cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon.” However, Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to developing a nuclear weapon this year that it was necessary to go to war, which he has made dozens of times in the past nine months, is undermined by public evidence and contradicts his own previous statements on US strikes against Iranian facilities in 2025. At a campaign rally in Alaska last month, Trump insisted that he had to join Israel in attacking Iran in February because, “they were two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon”. That claim appears at odds with what his then director of national intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, testified to Congress on 25 March 2025, two months into Trump’s second term: that US intelligence agencies reported that Iran had not tried to make a nuclear weapon for more than two decades. The US intelligence community, Gabbard said, “continues to assess Iran is not building a nuclear weapon and supreme leader Khamenei has not authorized the nuclear weapons program he suspended in 2003”. Despite that assessment, three months later, on 21 June 2025, Trump ordered the US bombing of Iran’s nuclear enrichment facilities. The strikes, Trump told the public that night , “were a spectacular military success. Iran’s key nuclear enrichment facilities have been completely and totally obliterated.” Eight months after that, however, when Trump announced the start of a full-scale war on Iran early on 28 February 2026, he said in a video statement from Mar-a-Lago the war was necessary to “ensure that Iran does not obtain a nuclear weapon”. The morning after this month’s midterm elections, Vance said in a statement posted on social media: “The reason we lost is the war.” “If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so,” he added. “Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost.” In the White House briefing room on Friday, after Trump said that Vance should have said the war was necessary, a reporter asked the vice-president whether he would argue that the war in Iran was worth it. In his response, Vance said it was not his place to second-guess the president, but refrained from actually endorsing Trump’s claim that the war was essential to stop Iran from creating a nuclear weapon. “Look, what I’ve said is the goal of keeping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon is absolutely what we need to be doing. It’s the biggest state sponsor of terrorism. If they had a nuclear weapon, they would use it as leverage or, God forbid, they would attack and kill thousands, hundreds of thousands, of innocent people,” Vance said. “I think the president is the one who makes the decision, and the president has said he would do it again.” “My view is that my goal is, and my job is, to support the president of the United States,” the vice-president said. The vice president’s office did not respond to a request to comment.

Strike on Russian cargo ship in Gulf of Finland 'likely carried out by Ukraine'
articles.body:
We reported earlier on a Russian cargo ship catching fire in the Gulf of Finland after a reported drone attack (see 10:35 post).

The Finnish Border Guard, who are leading the response to the incident, have now identified the affected ship as the Sparta II, a Russian vessel sanctioned by the US.

The force said the Sparta II was known to have links to Russian armed forces and that it couldn't rule out military material being on board the vessel.

The Sparta II crew are being evacuated, the border guard added.

A spokesperson for Finland's defence force said the strike on the vessel was likely carried out by Ukraine.

articles.title: Melania Trump says another ceasefire in Ukraine could happen 'before Christmas'
articles.summary: Melania Trump has suggested a new localised ceasefire in Ukraine could be agreed in the coming weeks
articles.body:
Melania Trump has suggested a new localised ceasefire in Ukraine could be agreed in the coming weeks.

Donald Trump's wife brokered the six-day ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky last month, when a humanitarian operation saw hundreds of citizens evacuated to Ukrainian-held territory.

She later brought Ukrainian and Russian officials together at the White House to mark the truce.

Asked on a Fox News special programme about her wishes for Christmas, the first lady said: "Well, it's world peace, of course, but first of all, I really would like to have more ceasefires.

"We could do it very fast if both Ukraine and Russia are willing. I am in talks already.

"So maybe we will have another ceasefire before Christmas."

In a social media post last week, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv has proposed 10 more areas in the Russian-controlled parts of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia where "a similar humanitarian operation" to Oleshky was needed.

articles.title: Drones attack cargo ship close to Russian border, Moscow says
articles.body:
A cargo ​vessel ‌heading to the Kaliningrad exclave was ​attacked by two drones in ⁠the Gulf of Finland, ‌a Russian official has said.

The governor of the Leningrad region, Aleksandr Drozdenko, said the vessel was struck by the drones in neutral waters, but was only three nautical miles from ‌Russia's border.

The ship's crew was evacuated ⁠after the incident.

The Finnish Border Guard, which shared an image of the vessel on fire, said it was preparing for "potential environmental damage" as it led the rescue operation.

Following the strike, the ship has drifted from international waters into Finnish territorial waters, it added.

The Gulf of Finland and Kaliningrad are Russia's only access points to the Baltic Sea, and have been regular targets for Ukrainian attacks.

St Petersburg, Russia's second-largest city, sits on the gulf's coast.

articles.title: Seven-year-old boy and paramedic killed in Russian strike on Zelenskyy's hometown
articles.summary: Two people have been killed in Russian ballistic missile strikes on the city of Kryvyi Rih overnight
articles.body:
Two people have been killed in Russian ballistic missile strikes on the city of Kryvyi Rih overnight.

Ukrainian broadcaster Suspilne reported the victims were a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old ambulance paramedic who arrived at the scene of the attack.

A further 60 people were injured in the attacks with around half hospitalised, as apartment buildings, a restaurant and a hospital were damaged in the city.

Russia's defence ministry said it struck a thermal power ​plant ⁠in the city.

Kryvyi Rih, in the Dnipropetrovsk region, is Volodymyr Zelenskyy's home town.

editorialRejections.title: Zelenskyy: Ukraine's NATO membership prospects depend on how war ends
editorialRejections.summary: The Ukrainian President emphasized that France and other allies understand that NATO membership is the clearest security guarantee for Ukraine
editorialRejections.reason: Local outlet reports an event outside its home country without a local subject
editorialRejections.body: Whether Ukraine will become a member of NATO depends on how the Russia-Ukraine war ends, and it is too early to make any definitive statements on the matter, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said during an online briefing via WhatsApp, UNIAN reports. Zelenskyy noted that Ukraine is considering the possibility of joining NATO and that the issue is also being discussed within the Alliance. According to him, the matter remains on the agenda and was also discussed at a meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" held in Berlin on November 19. The Ukrainian President emphasized that France and other allies understand that NATO membership is the clearest security guarantee for Ukraine. "France and other allies understand that the clearest security guarantee for Ukraine is NATO membership. And the most obvious way to strengthen NATO is to admit Ukraine to the Alliance and have an army like Ukraine's among its allies. Undoubtedly, this is in the interests of both sides – Ukraine and NATO," Zelenskyy said. It should be noted that the meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" held in Berlin on November 19 also addressed security guarantees for Ukraine, ending the war, and strengthening the country's defense capabilities.

editorialRejections.title: Refusal to cooperate with Russia in favor of EU brings Moldova to brink of bankruptcy
editorialRejections.summary: Europe’s globalist, expansionist ideas must be halted as here’s the striking example of our own small country
editorialRejections.reason: Local outlet reports an event outside its home country without a local subject
editorialRejections.body: MOSCOW, November 21. /TASS/. The Moldovan authorities led by President Maia Sandu have brought the country to the brink of bankruptcy by severing economic ties with Russia and seeking to replace them with cooperation with the European Union, Executive Committee Secretary of Moldova's Victory opposition bloc, a former member of the republic’s Parliament Marina Tauber told TASS. "Europe’s globalist, expansionist ideas must be halted as here’s the striking example of our own small country, which was once successful and prosperous, and fully capable of competing with other nations, in sectors like agriculture, winemaking, and many others, including industry," she said. The deterioration of economic ties with Russia is "worsening the living conditions" of the republic’s citizens in areas such as energy and pricing, Tauber stressed. "[In Moldova,] there is an economic crisis, which the current authorities have led us into because of their preference for the West . We are a bankrupt country," she noted. "They want to unite us with Romania, and they present this as being driven by some sort of noble intentions. How could one trade away one’s own sovereignty and independence for the sake of another country?" Tauber added. In her view, the Moldovan authorities are deliberately steering the country into such a state that unification with Romania will appear to be the only possible way out of the situation.

editorialRejections.title: Hungary plans to withdraw its blockade of Ukraine’s EU accession talks
editorialRejections.summary: This opens the possibility for Kyiv and Chisinau to begin negotiations on all membership chapters in the European Union, Euronews reported
editorialRejections.reason: Editor rejected this or a closely matching story
editorialRejections.body: After the long-standing blockade by Budapest, Hungary has agreed to withdraw its objections to the opening of the last two negotiating clusters with Ukraine, diplomatic sources confirmed. This opens the possibility for Kyiv and Chisinau to begin negotiations on all membership chapters in the European Union, Euronews reported. According to two diplomatic sources, Hungary plans to drop the veto at the meeting of the ambassadors of the EU member states. The intention was announced by Andras Biro-Nagy, state secretary for EU affairs, during the debate on enlargement in Brussels. Budapest had long blocked Ukraine’s candidacy, thereby also slowing the progress of Moldova, whose accession process was linked to the Ukrainian one. The change of position comes after Peter Magyar took power from Viktor Orban, who had been at the head of the Hungarian government for 16 years, Skopje1.mk reported. The first negotiating cluster was opened in June, the second in July, and the next two in October. Last month, Kyiv and Budapest reached an agreement on the rights of the Hungarian minority in western Ukraine, which was then adopted in the Ukrainian parliament. Although the Hungarian government announced readiness for the next step, the opening of the last two clusters was postponed for several weeks. Magyar and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy held their first bilateral meeting in Brussels on 16 October, on the margins of the European Council summit, which represented an additional step toward improving relations between the two neighboring countries. Among the clusters that are to be opened are also sensitive areas such as the environment and agriculture. Agriculture in particular will be an especially big challenge for Ukraine. The European Commission, under pressure from countries such as Poland and France, proposed restrictions on the access of certain Ukrainian agricultural products to the European market and EU funds. Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretky stated that Kyiv cannot accept the permanent exclusion of Ukrainian farmers from the European market and emphasized that any restrictions must be temporary and proportional. The opening of the negotiating clusters is only the beginning of the accession process. The candidates then have to align their laws and practices with European rules, and the EU member states have more than a hundred opportunities in the further phases to impose a veto and block progress.

The attack damaged a civilian business facility and a vehicle service station building. Seven vehicles were also damaged, including four passenger cars and three trucks. Roofs and windows of nearby private homes were also damaged. A fire broke out at the business facility but was extinguished by emergency responders. A power line was also damaged, and energy workers are working to restore electricity supply. As Ukrinform previously reported, three civilians were injured in Russian attacks in the Sumy region over the past 24 hours.

editorialRejections.title: US should explicitly state its desire to enter into peace agreement with Iran — Araghchi
editorialRejections.summary: We have not received any response from the American side
editorialRejections.reason: Local outlet reports an event outside its home country without a local subject
editorialRejections.body: TEHRAN, November 21. /TASS/. The United States must change its position and state a clear intention to reach a peace agreement with Iran in order to begin negotiations on opening the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in an interview with the newspaper Iran. "We have not received any response from the American side. Therefore, if they are truly serious about reaching an agreement, it is only natural that we would first expect them to change their position," he said, commenting on a recent statement by US leader Donald Trump that the United States no longer needs a deal with the republic. Tehran is demanding that Washington explicitly state its desire to conclude a peace agreement and adopt a set of confidence-building measures between the two sides, the minister added. If the American side fulfills these two conditions, Iran is prepared to discuss the draft agreement and its implementation, he noted. "Our demand is perfectly clear: for the Strait of Hormuz to be opened, seven conditions we have put forward must be met. Of course, if the Americans have any proposals or opinions regarding the fulfillment of these conditions, we are prepared to discuss them. If Iran’s demands are met, the Strait of Hormuz will be opened. Even if it becomes necessary to discuss the details and ways to implement these conditions, we are ready to enter into negotiations at the expert level," Araghchi stressed. Iran is also prepared for negotiations regarding its enriched uranium stockpiles, he said, adding though that Tehran insists that nuclear materials must not leave the country.
